#3491. Casting Director Francine Maisler on ‘Dune: Part Three’

When Denis Villeneuve brought on seasoned casting director Francine Maisler for the first Dune movie, they were starting from scratch. For the ambitious adaptation of Frank Herbert’s 1965 sci-fi novel, they had to cast not only the lead character, Paul Atreides, but dozens of other main characters—powerful warriors, scheming royals, shape-shifting conspirators—to inhabit the world.

Luckily, the pair had already worked together on Villeneuve’s three previous films, Sicario, Blade Runner 2049, and Arrival. “Denis’s vision is my compass,” Maisler tells Vanity Fair. “His passion [for Dune] since he was a teen was all I needed to follow.”

When they were casting the first installment, Maisler was aware that it was possible that these actors might play these characters for more than just one film. “I did have an idea that they would have to have the presence and the acting talent to be able to carry this potentially for three movies,” she says.

Dune (2021), starring Timothée Chalamet as Paul Atreides and Zendaya as Chani, was just the first step. Maisler returned to cast Dune: Part Two (2024), and Dune: Part Three, which will wrap up Villeneuve’s trilogy when it hits theaters on December 18.

Maisler is a titan of casting, having worked on hundreds of films with filmmakers such as Luca Guadagnino, Greta Gerwig, Aaron Sorkin, Paul Greengrass, Adam McKay, and Terrence Malick, and she was nominated for the first casting Oscar in 2026 for her work on Ryan Coogler’s Sinners.

The casting Oscar didn’t exist when she began working on the Dune franchise, but this installment is likely to draw attention from the Academy. Over the three films, the cast has grown into an incredible ensemble, packed with many of today’s biggest movie stars, along with well-known veterans and a few unexpected choices. “One thing about Denis is if ever I bring him a name and he likes it, and I’ll say, ‘Well, do you want to hire that actor?’ He says to me something I think is so poetic,” says Maisler. “He says, ‘Francine, let me get back to you tomorrow. I need to dream about it.’”

Ahead of the release of Dune: Part Three, Maisler looks back at casting the trilogy’s most important roles, including the exciting new additions to the upcoming film—and the possibility of more Dune in the future.

In Herbert’s book, Atreides is a slender 15-year-old with dark hair. “To find a 15-year-old who had that talent to carry this whole movie, we weren’t sure was out there,” remembers Maisler. The name that came up was then 22-year-old Chalamet, whom Maisler had previously cast in Hostiles, Beautiful Boy, The King, and Little Women. Chalamet, who didn’t have to audition but did meet with Villeneuve, would have to play Atreides from a young man who then begins to amass power in the second film and, after a 12-year time jump, is burdened with the choices he’s made waging a galactic war in the third. Though Chalamet hadn’t led a big blockbuster before, Maisler saw the depth of his talent. “I do think Beautiful Boy showed me the depth of Timothée as an actor, as a young man, and that this was the next step in his progression as an actor, that he was able to hold a franchise in his hand,” says Maisler.

There was a worldwide search for Chani, the skilled Fremen warrior from Arrakis who falls in love with Atreides. At the time, Zendaya was in the middle of filming the first season of Euphoria, and her graduation from Disney star to movie star had not yet happened. Zendaya screen tested with Chalamet, which sealed it for Maisler and Villeneuve. “She came in with five other incredibly talented actresses, but the minute you saw her with Timothée in a room, you just knew that there’s something special happening,” she says. “She has such power when she walks in the room, and she’s breathtaking in the most interesting way.”

Of course, Paul Atreides’s parents, Duke Leto Atreides and Lady Jessica, needed to look like Chalamet, but Maisler started with the characters’ essences when casting. Duke Leto Atreides was considered a fair and devoted leader as the noble head of House Atreides. Maisler saw that gravitas in Oscar Isaac. Lady Jessica becomes a force in the story because of her heightened physical and mental control as a trained member of the Bene Gesserit sisterhood. “Rebecca is so powerful, isn’t she?” says Maisler. “She really, I have to say, surprised me. I always knew how talented she was, but she just owned that part.”

Villeneuve and Maisler had worked with Brolin on the 2015 crime thriller Sicario. Maisler, who calls Brolin “one of our greatest actors,” was excited to have him back, this time playing Gurney Halleck, the Warmaster of House Atreides and a mentor to Paul Atreides. The character is described in the book as a warrior-poet, requiring strength and depth. “He’s so charismatic, so masculine,” says Maisler of Brolin. “He’s kind of a throwback from other generations.”

When Momoa’s agent brought up Momoa’s name, Maisler wasn’t quite sure about the idea because at the time he was known for starring in the DC movie franchise as Aquaman. “I was a bit skeptical, I have to admit, because I knew he had this incredible presence on screen, but I didn’t know, truly, his talent, and that’s taught me a lot about being open to people who come from different types of films,” she says. Villeneuve was more open to the idea at the start, and met with him about playing Duncan Idaho, a fierce fighter and protector of Paul Atreides. He returns in the third movie as a ghola—a sort of clone—named Hayt, which demands a more complicated performance from Momoa. “Jason’s an incredible artist, and I’ve come to just love him,” says Maisler. “He’s so funny. I want to put him in a romantic comedy next, because he really is one of the big surprises in the ensemble.”

Taylor-Joy had already risen in stardom by the time she joined the franchise for the second film. Her breakout was in The Witch, and she starred in hit series The Queen's Gambit, which earned her a Golden Globe and a SAG Award. This made it slightly surprising that Alia Atreides, Paul’s volatile sister, makes a blink-and-you’ll-miss-it appearance in the second film. “I give her a lot of credit for not counting lines in the second one,” says Maisler, who says Taylor-Joy signed on for the second because of the potential of the third installment. Indeed, in Dune: Part Three, Alia is a loyal sister and vengeful force who is not afraid to get blood on her hands. Taylor-Joy’s charisma and intensity will jump off the screen, says Maisler. “Actors are very smart, and they know when to trust a director like Denis,” she says. “When he says there is going to be something in the third film and he describes it, he will make it happen.”

A tribal leader of the desert-dwelling Fremen, Stilgar is a seasoned warrior and becomes a devout follower of Paul Atreides as Muad’Dib. The role required a level of intensity. “Oh, I think we all just prayed that Javier would do it,” says Maisler. “I think every actor wants to work with Javier, and he’s one of probably a handful of actors I think can do anything.”

Pugh joined for the second film as well, but like Taylor-Joy, she didn’t have a ton to do. But Princess Irulan, who marries Paul Atreides as a political union, is a key part of the plot in Dune: Part Three, joining a conspiracy against Paul. Maisler first saw Pugh in the 2016 film Lady Macbeth, and then cast her as Amy March in Gerwig’s Little Women. “You saw on that what an intelligent actress she is, and singular,” she says. “She knows no boundaries, and she’s confident and bold.” She says Pugh has always reminded her of Debra Winger, the star of An Officer and a Gentleman (1982), and Terms of Endearment (1983). “She’s just commanding, and she has this energy, and everything she does is fascinating,” says Maisler. “You can’t take your eyes off of her.”

The third installment brings in yet another major star with Pattinson, who plays Scytale, a shape-shifter who is conspiring to dethrone Paul Atreides. Maisler, who also worked with Pattinson in Primetime, which also came out this year, describes him as “one of the versatile actors in his choices.” She had also worked with Pattinson on Mickey 17, which proved that he could play many different versions of a character—a skill that would be required of him in this third Dune movie. “Robert's a tremendous actor, and I think he takes these really bold chances,” says Maisler. As for his recent announcement as the next James Bond, Maisler has faith he and Villeneuve will deliver. “I think the way Denis and Rob created the character in Dune: Part Three together speaks to the surprises that we will see in Bond,” she says.

For Dune: Part Three, Maisler and Villeneuve had to find two actors who looked like twins and also looked like the offspring of Chalamet and Zendaya. They initially hoped to cast real twins, but didn’t find the right pair. In the end, they found their Ghanima and Leto II in Ida Brooke and Nakoa-Wolf Momoa. Brooke, who looks strikingly like Zendaya, is a relative newcomer who previously appeared on Apple’s sci-fi drama Silo (which stars Rebecca Ferguson). And Nakoa-Wolf Momoa, who makes his feature acting debut in Dune: Part Three, is Jason Momoa’s son—though Maisler didn’t know that when she first watched his audition tape. “Then came this tape of this young man who had incredible presence, and—we didn’t ask for this—he added some combat footage to his tape,” she says. Maisler says sometimes actors will call in a favor to get their child an audition, but Wolf, as she calls him, got this on his own. This casting was the most important for the third film because of what might be to come. “It was almost like casting the first one where these two young actors could go on to potentially, if there’s another movie where they’re leads,” says Maisler. There have been no official announcements of any future Dune movies, but for those mourning the end of the Villeneuve trilogy, Maisler is planting a small seed of hope here. The third Dune book, Children of Dune, centers on Leto and Ghanima, which means the two young actors Maisler found may have more story ahead of them.

#3490. There's Actually a Simple Explanation for All These Widespread Outages

It feels like every time you look at your phone lately, another company is having an outage. Last week, there was Microsoft, whose outage took down services from Outlook to Teams. Then, the FAA grounded all flights across the U.S. following "communication issues." This week, a number of banks experienced outages, as did Apple. Even the NSA's internal communications network went dark. Some of the biggest corporations and organizations in the world can't seem to keep their services running, leading to widespread disruptions and confusion. When it's a one-off, it's an annoyance; when it's outage after outage, it starts to feel like a pattern.

That pattern, in turn, has begun to fuel anxiety among the general public. What could possibly be causing Apple, Microsoft, JP Morgan Chase, and the NSA alike to go dark at roughly the same time? Is it a coordinated cyberattack? An AI revolt? Is the end finally nigh? To an outside observer, it certainly appears like something coordinated and nefarious is happening here. Secretary of State Marco Rubio is insistent that there is "zero evidence" that hackers or bad actors caused any of these outages, and President Trump is particularly unconcerned by the whole ordeal, saying, "It's life," and "Things like that happen."

But to skeptics of the U.S. government, these trickles of information aren't necessarily reassuring. While I agree with calls for someone from the government (perhaps the president himself) to make an official announcement explaining the situation, the root cause does appear to be clear at this time: The short answer? AI is at fault here, but not in the way you think.

Love it or hate it, AI is a force to be reckoned with. While you might know that AI can generate hyper-realistic videos and manage your emails on your behalf, certain models are adept at discovering new security vulnerabilities in software. These models aren't just helpful tools; they far surpass the abilities of human researchers. You might remember Anthropic initially pulled the brakes on its breakthrough model, Claude Mythos, when it found that the model could root out security vulnerabilities in just about anything.

Mythos, and models like it, are a double-edged sword. On the one hand, they can be major assets for developers and researchers to find new security vulnerabilities that humans otherwise wouldn't have discovered, and patch them accordingly. Unfortunately, the same can be said for bad actors, who can use these models to learn about new security flaws and attempt to exploit them before researchers have a chance to find them. As such, software developers across the spectrum, from small-time devs to major corporations, have been racing to patch as many security vulnerabilities as they can find—and they're finding a lot.

You might notice your PC's security updates, for example, are shipping with more patches than usual—historic levels, even. Microsoft keeps breaking its own records with its Patch Tuesday updates, including over 1,400 fixes with its October update. The company's October 2025 Patch Tuesday update, by comparison, included fewer than 180 fixes.

It's important to understand that just about every company that develops software is furiously working to patch its systems before hackers or AI agents exploit vulnerabilities first. And while there are successes (Microsoft is now protecting its customers from thousands of flaws each month), this speed is also inadvertently breaking things along the way. That's not just speculation: According to The Washington Sun, both Wall Street executives and the NSA explained to members of Congress that patching security flaws discovered by AI models caused this week's widespread outages.

Barring some campaign to cover up a coordinated attack on systems and services, it does seem like these outages are simply the result of companies breaking their own products in an attempt to stop AI-assisted hackers from exploiting undiscovered flaws. But that's not all that reassuring, either. AI models are only going to keep getting better at finding vulnerabilities; likewise, AI agents are only improving at hacking into systems autonomously. Companies will need to ramp up their efforts to patch their software before both hackers and AI agents discover those flaws first, and so the cycle will continue. Unless something changes, we may see routine outages as companies try to fix things as quickly as possible.

The implications aren't specific to any one company, either. Our world increasingly relies on fewer companies to keep us all connected. We saw that last year, when cloud hosting providers like AWS and Cloudflare each experienced outages. When these services go down, so do all of the networks that rely on them. If AWS or Cloudflare break something while trying to patch their systems, whole parts of the internet go dark.

Of course, it'll only be more difficult for the general public—if not the developers themselves—to recognize when outages are the result of maintenance or a cyberattack. Just because recent outages don't appear to be nefarious in nature, that doesn't mean future outages will be so innocent. For the time being, however, it seems we can worry less about an active cybersecurity incident, and more about how AI is disrupting modern life in ways few of us saw coming.

Scroll down for everything to know about Brassel:

WWE moved away from Survivor Series’ traditional format of all multi-man matches in the mid 90s. I get where Vince McMahon and company were coming from. It’s harder to build when you have so many moving parts, and it was harder to get people to buy PPVs back in the day without world title matches. In an effort to get back to the spirit of Survivor Series, Triple H has used a men’s and women’s WarGames match the last few years to keep that 5 on 5 format, but the event doesn't have quite the same prestige it once did. This year, however, he also threw in an old school Survivor Series elimination match, and the build has been the best thing on WWE television in months.

Seriously, if you have not been watching the segments for the United States versus Mexico match over the past several weeks, you have missed out big time. Cody Rhodes was picked as captain of the United States team. He quickly added CM Punk, who promptly appointed himself as co-captain. Since then, they’ve been trying to fill out the roster, and it’s led to a nice showcase for team members LA Knight and Je’Von Evans, as well as a fun segment with proposed team member The Miz and maybe the best segment of the entire year with a 70-something year old Hacksaw Jim Duggan who joined the team and then promptly quit after seeing a highlight reel of their Mexican opponents. I cannot freaking wait for the match, especially after Seth Rollins was added to maximize the drama.

Fortunately, there are some other exciting matches to look forward to, as well. The men’s War Games will feature the Bloodline against the 946, the latter of whom feel like they’re building some real momentum and are an actual threat to win. The women’s War Games match hasn’t had quite the same build, but it still features some top talent and should be a good showcase for younger talent as well. Throw in a pretty compelling Women’s World Championship match with Liv Morgan and Becky Lynch, and the card is really pretty solid.

Before I get into what I think is going to happen in each match, you can check out how I’ve done on predictions. I’ve given my take ahead of every PLE since WrestleMania 38, and while I’m not going to main event WrestleMania with this win-loss record, I could be competing for a midcard championship. Here’s a quick snapshot of the bigger WWE PLEs this year, as well as the overall record…

With all due respect to Team Mexico and especially Penta who currently holds the Money In The Bank Briefcase, this match is lopsided on paper. Cody, CM Punk and Seth are three of the biggest stars in the entire company, and Rhdoes especially does not lose unless it’s in a very key spot or in service of building to something larger or very memorably at WrestleMania 39, both. This match, however, feels like it’s really building toward something larger. It feels like a Mega Powers explode situation.

There’s been so much talk about Cody Rhodes possibly turning heel after punting Randy Orton, but I think it’s more likely we’re going to see CM Punk turn on Cody, or potentially turn full heel, as he’s clearly irate about Rhodes adding his longtime enemy Seth Rollins to the team. At minimum, the story of this match is going to be about the simmering tension between Rhodes, Punk and Rollins. Now, does that mean they’re going to actually lose the match? Not necessarily.

They could fight amongst themselves and wind up with some shock eliminations, or they could fight through the tension and win, pushing the inevitable turn further down the road.

I feel like the long-term goal here is to move us into a feud with Liv Morgan and Roxanne Perez. Rumors have swirled that Perez was originally slated to win Money In The Bank. She appeared in Morgan’s backstage segment with her this past Monday. Lynch has talked about how Judgment Day is holding her back. She’s clearly going to play a factor here in some way. It would be easy to say she’ll turn on Morgan and cost her the belt, but I don’t think that’s going to happen.

First, I don’t think there’s been enough teasing of a Judgment Day break-up. Fans have speculated about it forever, but we haven’t gotten nearly enough friction since Finn left to maximize the possible payoff here. Doing it now would be underbaked and stupid. Second, I think what Roxanne actually wants is a shot at the title, and she’s going to ruin that if Morgan loses the title. So, I think she’s going to help her ensure Liv keeps it.

Throw in the fact that Liv is already committed to the John Cena classic, and I feel pretty confident she’s going to hold onto the belt here.

For the longest time, I was sure we were headed toward an Alexa Bliss and Charlotte Flair break-up, but curiously, WWE really hasn’t teased much friction between the two lately, not since Tatum Paxley's early main roster promotion. Without that dynamic, this really just feels like a run of the mill babyfaces vs heels match that we would get at a house show.

Maybe there’s an angle I’m not seeing here or one that will emerge during the show, but absent that, I’m going to pick the babyfaces because when in doubt, always pick the babyfaces. That’s just a standard wrestling rule, and given I think there’s a potential for a lot of heels to win on this card, it makes even more sense to go with the babyfaces.

Predicted Winner: Charlotte Flair, Alexa Bliss, Tatum Paxley, Stephanie Vaquer and Bayley.

This is the moment where we find out how WWE really feels about 946 and Royce Keys. They’ve been the primary antagonists on the show for months and have been presented like really dangerous and unhinged monsters we should take seriously. If they lose here, it kind of feels like that’s the end. I mean I’m not saying they’re going to get released, but it feels like that’s the end of the audience taking them seriously. They’re the ones stepping up and trying to prove they’re main event players. If they lose in their first big PLE match trying to do that, then that tells the audience all they need to know.

I think WWE believes in them more than that. I think they also believe in the recently added Cruz Montana, and I think they see the 946 as another chance to push Carmelo. They really need this win in a way the Bloodline doesn’t, and if they do win, it would make all the sense in the world to build toward Keys getting a legit title shot at Royal Rumble against Roman Reigns. He would be a big underdog in that match, but he would at least be coming off some momentum from a victory here.

I think the 946 really needs to win, but WWE also almost never has the Bloodline actually lose. So, do I feel confident about this? No.

#3484. Decoding Kate Middleton’s “Tourdrobe” for Her Trip to India

When Kate Middleton stepped out on the green carpet at the Earthshot Awards ceremony in Mumbai this week, it was “an absolute princess moment,” says British designer Amanda Wakeley.

“Catherine has really come into her own. She has found her stride and a new confidence, and you see that in this dazzling but also practical ‘tourdrobe,’’’ Wakeley, who has previously dressed the Princess of Wales and used to dress Princess Diana, tells Vanity Fair.

It has been 10 years since Princess Kate last visited India. Her fashion choices are more sophisticated now than on her visit in 2016, and the speech she delivered at the Earthshot Prize ceremony on November 17 shows a new confidence. With her elevated look, there’s no trace of High Street labels. Kate’s flared floral dresses and the wedge shoes she used to love (but the late Queen Elizabeth apparently disliked) have been replaced by Manolo Blahnik pumps, couture power suits, and clothes by some of her favorite designers, such as Emilia Wickstead.

Prince William and Princess Kate attend The Earthshot Prize Awards Ceremony at the Jio World Convention Centre on November 17, 2026 in Mumbai, India.

Kate’s decision to wear a striking vermilion dress made from handwoven silk by New Delhi–based designer Mahima Mahajan to the Earthshot Prize ceremony spoke volumes. The eye-catching dress, which she paired with a burgundy Prada velvet clutch, was chosen after Kate had selected a special suite of emeralds from the royal gem collection. The green stones on the dress perfectly matched her jewels, which served as an homage to both Queen Elizabeth II and India, as the green of the Indian flag represents growth and prosperity.

The dazzling stones known as the “emerald tassel suite” were worn frequently by the late Queen Elizabeth II, and while Kate has previously worn the earrings, this marked the first time she wore the set. The effect was dramatic.

“Never has Catherine looked more like a queen in waiting,” Wakeley says of the look.

Wearing the suite ensured that Kate, who has free rein of the royal jewels, looked more regal than ever. “What was fascinating was seeing Catherine wear these incredible family heirlooms along with more relaxed collections from some of her favorite modern jewelry designers like Kiki McDonough and Astley Clarke,” remarks Wakeley.

Kate’s carefully curated wardrobe for the trip wasn’t just about power dressing—it was also about showing she can be sustainable as well as on trend.

“It was good to see Catherine making a proper nod to sustainability by rewearing her Roksanda dress,” Wakeley notes. “It’s clear a lot of thought has gone into her outfit choices. Her wardrobe has to be practical, and her clothes have to work harder than most people consider for their clothing; she needs weight in the hem of the floaty dresses. She has learned lessons the hard way. She is often seen bending down, talking to children, so she’s conscious of how low a neckline is, how short a skirt is.”

Princess Kate visits the Nowrosjee Wadia Maternity Hospital, on November 18, 2026 in Mumbai, India.

For her visit to Mumbai’s Nowrosjee Wadia Maternity Hospital on November 18, Catherine chose a striking red tailored Emilia Wickstead skirt suit with Manolo Blahnik pumps. On November 16, she opted for a pistachio blazer by designer Veronica Beard, paired with white Alexander McQueen trousers and pearl-buckled Camilla Elphick flats, a relaxed and accessible look for when she picked up a cricket bat.

Princess Kate plays cricket on November 16, 2026 in Mumbai, India.

As Princess of Wales, Catherine is often compared to Princess Diana. “The main difference is Diana was a fashion icon. Catherine has become a style icon,” Wakeley says. “There’s a big difference. Diana played into the fashion of the day and was finding her style. During the time she resigned from public life, she worked out her style DNA. Catherine has had to do that on the job. Very wisely, she has worked out her style and doesn’t get too impacted by fashion and trends. She goes for what she likes. What works for her rather than trends. She really knows now what works for her.”

#3483. Another Gaming Console Price Hike Could Be Coming, Thanks To New Tariffs

The US government has announced a new round of tariffs targeting several major countries, including China, Japan, Vietnam, and European Union trading partners. Under the proposed tariffs, import taxes will rise significantly, with China facing up to 40% when the new duties take effect next year. According to the BBC, some of the rates will be reduced because of tariff caps that US President Donald Trump has already agreed to, and individual countries could also face different levies.

What does this mean for gaming hardware? Trump's first round of "Liberation Day" tariffs contributed to rising console prices, but the Supreme Court eventually struck them down. Big companies like Sony, Microsoft, and Nintendo benefited from tariff refunds after the ruling, but they didn't pass the savings on to consumers. In Sony's case, it was estimated to get back $508 million in refunds from the US government.

The new tariffs bypass the Supreme Court's ruling by using a different law, Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, which allows the government to impose tariffs on countries that use unfair business practices. The law does require an investigation into specific trade practices before rates are set. If higher import taxes take effect, console companies could face much higher costs, and protecting their profits will likely mean consumers have to cover the difference.

Nintendo, Sony, and Microsoft have moved much of their final assembly out of China and into Southeast Asia, especially Vietnam, to avoid earlier tariffs. However, key parts like batteries and power supplies still mostly come from China, and if tariffs on these parts rise, total production costs for consoles made outside China will go up even more.

Some electronic goods could be exempt from tariffs, and manufacturers often stockpile inventory ahead of tariff deadlines to delay price changes. But with rising costs from the ongoing components shortage amid the AI boom and other global factors, console prices remain at risk. After the June announcement of steep console price hikes, Microsoft warned that Xbox console costs could rise again in 2027, and next-gen hardware is also expected to be very pricey.

Bia was previously linked to Olivia Rodrigo and Charli D’Amelio, while Earle dated MLB player Tyler Wade for three months in 2022 before moving on with NFL wide receiver Braxton Berrios the next year. After the influencer and Berrios, 31, split in late 2025, she briefly dated Tom Brady earlier this year.

Now that Earle is single once more, it’s admittedly been challenging to find The One.

“I mean, my life is always out there,” the Earle Meets World star exclusively told Us in August. “I think when it comes to dating and stuff, there’s moments where things are put out there before I necessarily would want them out there — and not that I’m dating anyone, but you’re standing next to someone and all of a sudden it’s a big story, and I think that’s hard to navigate.”

“That’s been tricky,” she acknowledged. “But, I mean, well, I guess we’ll see what happens.”

While navigating the dating scene, Earle holds no ill will against her exes like Berrios. They were even cordial after running into one another at the 2026 Miami Grand Prix.

“It wasn’t awkward between them at all,” a second source told Us in May. “Alix was genuinely happy to see Braxton and say hello. There is no bad blood between them, and they have both moved on.”

Per the second insider, the reunion brought up “mixed emotions” for Earle.

“Like anyone, of course it brings up mixed emotions for Alix, but she feels like she is in a good place mentally right now,” the source noted at the time. “There are no thoughts on rekindling with Braxton. He was super friendly toward her and not cold in the slightest.”

#3481. GTA 6’s Mandy Actor Reacts To The Online “Weirdos”

One of the most talked-about characters in GTA 6 outside of Jason and Lucia has been Mandy, a woman who tries to seduce Jason early in the game. She may also be a serial killer. The actor who plays Mandy, Lexie Shoaibi, has now discussed how she got the part and her reaction to people being weird online.

Speaking to Vulture, Shoaibi said she's able to see "more good than bad" thanks to her experience being a content creator.

"There are weirdos out there, and they’re going to try to bring you down, so it’s important to stay around the people and the places that aren’t doing that," she said. "It’s easy enough to do, which I’m very grateful for. There’s enough support in my real-life community and online that I can say, 'I could just hang out over here. I don’t actually need to go to the scary place.' I’m living in the positive, for sure."

People have been, to put it mildly, thirsting over Mandy since GTA 6 came out. However, Shoaibi had no idea she was going to be in GTA 6 at all because when she auditioned, she signed what she described as an "incredibly" strict NDA. In fact, she didn't even know what she was auditioning for.

Her commercial agent in New York brought it to her, and she thought it would be "just like any other commercial audition." From the time she auditioned until the game launched on November 19, Shoaibi did not know she was going to be in GTA 6. Instead, she did the audition and recorded her scenes for a project she knew as "Project Bubblegum."

Shoaibi said the notes she received included being told to play a “sexy ex-girlfriend" and to "be seductive.” 

When Shoaibi finally saw Mandy in GTA 6, she said it was "very exciting," in part because it meant that Rockstar didn't cut it. She did the recording for Mandy in 2023 or early 2024, Shoaibi said, and now that GTA 6 is finally here and her role as Mandy confirmed, Shoaibi said, "I feel like I'm living in a dream. It's crazy."

Shoaibi said she hopes her role as Mandy in the biggest video game ever can help grow her profile and get more jobs. "There’s definitely momentum that I wasn’t feeling before," she said.

GTA 6 launched on November 19 and had a gigantic debut, selling 32.5 million copies by launch and generating around $4 billion on day one.

For more, check out GameSpot’s GTA 6 review and our rundown of five things to do first.

#3478. Wondering If There Were ‘Red Flags’ For Theranos Employees? A Former Assistant Spoke Out

A Former Theranos Employee Watched You Can See Everything. What He Saw Made Him Want To Scream At The Screen

Elizabeth Holmes’ Partner Wants To Set The Record Straight On New Business NOT Being ‘Theranos 3’

Nathan Fielder Had One Ask For Elizabeth Holmes’ Documentary, And I’d Never Heard Of This Happening

Unlock instant access to exclusive member features.

Get full access to premium articles, exclusive features and a growing list of member rewards.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The Nathan Fielder/Lance Oppenheim co-directed hit documentary You Can See Everything, which has done huge box office numbers on the 2026 movie schedule, does a very deep dive into Elizabeth Holmes after Theranos. Now, everyone from former employees to psychologists is weighing in on Holmes both before and after her fraud convictions led to a long prison sentence that she is currently serving in Texas. Recently, one of Holmes’ assistants, Aria Marinelli, from the early days of Theranos, appeared on the Assistants vs. Agents podcast and spoke about a few red flags she saw in her short time working for the disgraced CEO.

Marinelli worked for Holmes at Theranos in 2009, which lands right in the middle of the company’s history, which was founded in 2003 and collapsed in 2016 before going completely out of business in 2018. Holmes went to prison in 2023. Marinelli wasn’t at the company long, by the sound of things, but did work directly for Holmes in her time with the Silicon Valley startup that promised big things with what we now know was a completely fraudulent blood-testing machine (a machine Marinelli says she never even laid eyes on until seeing You Can See Everything).

In the interview, she highlights a few things that made her question whether she wanted to be part of the company and if what they were doing was legitimate. According to Marinelli, the suspicions started even before she accepted the job, as she explained:

I went and looked through old emails just to see if I was remembering correctly, and it turns out I was. So this is [an email to] a mentor of mine. I said: ‘It's looking like I have to get Theranos an answer tomorrow regarding their offer. It expires at COB, and they've already extended it once. I'm very hesitant to accept because the work and the work environment are really not my ideal next step. Something about it doesn't sit right, I guess.’

She went on to explain that pretty early on, there was never a lot of talk about what the company was trying to do with the machine. In typical Silicon Valley style, according to Marinelli, most of the talk was about stock shares, IPOs, and how much money they could all make. That was something else that didn’t sit right with her.

Not only did Marinelli never see the now-infamous device, but she never saw a blood testing lab at all and was worried that despite famous names on the board of directors, there seemed to be no one with medical knowledge. That also raised concerns for her, as she explained:

The biggest thing was that there was no lab. So I had noticed that there were no doctors on the board, and that's, again, been talked about ad nauseam, but I was willing to dismiss that as maybe they were just getting started, right? And I remember just being told, ‘Oh, it's off-site,’ but I never saw anybody in that time frame that was working in a lab or that was from that lab.

The final straw for Marinelli was when she was tasked with tracking down one of the company’s machines from the Army, which was supposedly testing it. Through multiple emails and phone calls, she seemed to be a wild goose chase, with everyone pointing to other people, and no one knowing where the device actually was. Marinelli told host Warner Bailey:

Everyone [at Theranos] is very secretive, very, you know, shielded in how they're speaking about this thing. I doubt they would just ship it off to someone and not have them have a concerted program around testing it.  So that, to me, was kind of the last flag that I was willing to put up with.

Marinelli also gave her honest impression of Holmes, and it wasn’t all negative, but she did mention that she thought The Dropout, the series starring Amanda Seyfried that can be seen with a Hulu subscription, is a fair portrayal of Holmes as Marinelli knew her. She also praised You Can See Everything and seems to have real sympathy for Holmes, saying, “everyone has to lie at that level.”

One of the many interesting and brilliant things about You Can See Everything is that everyone sees something different in it, including the people who worked for Holmes and Theranos, and I don’t think this is the last time we’ll hear from people who worked with her and knew her. Especially as this movie continues to get Oscar buzz and will continue to be in the cultural zeitgeist for some time.

#3477. Diablo 4 Is Making Helltides A Hell Of A Lot Easier

One of Diablo 4's oldest endgame activities, Helltides, is getting a major refresh for Season 16.

As detailed by developer Blizzard in their full breakdown of Season of Tyrael's Gambit, Helltides will soon be far more efficient to run than before. The whole point of the activity is to kill as many demons as fast as possible, acquire the Aberrant Cinders they drop, and then use those cinders to open chests for items.

Dying means losing half of the cinders you've collected, but they are also lost when the Helltide ends. Oftentimes that means having left over amounts of cinders you can't spend, only to then go to the next Helltide five minutes later and repeat the process from zero. It's been this way since Diablo 4 launched back in 2023.

In Season 16, that will finally change. Blizzard is getting rid of the downtime between Helltides spawning and making it so there will always be a Helltide up in one of the game's original zones, as well as one in expansion areas like Hahantu or Skovos. Even better, Aberrant Cinders won't be lost once a Helltide ends. Instead, players can collect up to 5,000 cinders at a time to be spent on opening chests within the activity. Additionally, the overall loot quality from opening chests in the Helltide will be improved and chests can be opened instantly.

Those changes should go a long way towards making Helltides feel more valuable and efficient when trying to farm gear, as you can now blast demons to your heart's content until reaching the Aberrant Cinder cap. Just don't die while you have a full 5,000 stored up. 

Diablo 4 Season 16 launches December 1. Alongside its Helltide changes, the season will bring big updates to War Plans as well. A new system, War Plans Tactics, will give players more control over what activities appear in their War Plans, as well as more options when it comes to rerolling them and the rewards they grant. Players will also have new Horadric items to chase that will modify specific Talisman sets, greatly increasing their power. 

Blizzard additionally announced many of the features that were added as part of Diablo 4 Season 15, Hell's Legacy, will be made permanent. Those additions include the season's capstone dungeons, optional bosses like Moophisto, the Annihilus Seal, Hellfire Torch Charm, and the season's legacy Unique items like Stone of Jordan.

#3476. Michelle Randolph Makes Rare Comment About Sister Cassie's 'Bachelor' Journey

Michelle Randolph made a rare comment about sister Cassie Randolph‘s tumultuous time on The Bachelor.

“We jokingly told her, ‘You’re single, you’re young, go on the show.’ Not thinking twice about it,” Michelle, 29, recalled during an interview with The Hollywood Reporter, which was published on Tuesday, November 24.

Cassie, 31, appeared on season 23 of The Bachelor in 2019 amid Colton Underwood‘s search for love. Underwood, 34, infamously hopped a fence away from the cameras after Cassie chose to leave the season early instead of getting engaged.

The pair got back together off screen and dated for a year. Us confirmed in September 2020 that Cassie was granted a restraining order against Underwood after she claimed he had been stalking and harassing her. The case was dropped in November 2020, and Underwood came out as gay the following year.

“It was a crazy time,” Michelle told THR. “It was pretty overwhelming to be thrown into a world like that — the social media of it all.”

The Landman actress struggled with the online commentary, adding, “People online were so beyond cruel. Sometimes I just want to black it out. Bachelor Nation is … well, it’s a lot.”

Before Michelle’s profile came out, Underwood revealed whether he’s on speaking terms with Cassie.

“I have no contact. If she ever did reach out or want to reach out, I would be open to answering any questions that her or her family would have for me,” he told Vanity Fair in February. “That is something I’ve always offered. I’m in no position to really say much more than that or reach out. There’s been no part of me that would. I would always be up for it. It’s all on her terms.”

Underwood, who married husband Jordan C. Brown in May 2023 before welcoming a son together, continued: “I will always own the mistakes that I made. I will always feel guilt and feel this extreme sadness for how I showed up for certain friends, for people in my life. Also fans — letting people down. At that point, people had been sort of invested in me and in my story. So I did feel like not only I let myself down, I let a lot of people down there.”

Cassie, meanwhile, recently spoke to Us about life out of the spotlight after finding love with husband Brighton Reinhardt, whom she wed in December 2025.

“[The] best part [of being married] is we just have so much fun together,” she gushed earlier this month. “We always want to hang out and talk and chat and spill the tea.”

#3475. Why GTA 6 Doesn’t Let You Replay Missions–It Felt “Alien And Disconnected”

One of the first things people noticed with Grand Theft Auto 6 is that you cannot replay missions, at least not in a simple, straightforward way. GTA 5 had a mission replay option, as did Red Dead Redemption II, so why doesn't GTA 6?

Senior design director Scott Butchard told Kotaku that Rockstar "certainly" considered a mission replay feature "early on in development." However, Butchard said, "As the game came together, it felt at odds with the story we were trying to tell and felt a bit alien and disconnected."

He went on to say replaying missions "really diminished the choices you had made."

While GTA 6 doesn't make it easy to replay missions, you still can do so by reloading an earlier GTA 6 save. Something else to know is that if you're in the middle of a mission and it's not going to plan, you can open the game menu and select retry, quit, or restart.

GTA 6 blasted off with 32.5 million sales via prepurchases alone and around $4 billion in revenue on day one. The game is only going to get bigger and sell more copies over time, and it's helping drive new PlayStation and Xbox hardware sales.

In other GTA 6 news, the actor who plays the character Mandy has reacted to people being weird online. Rockstar has also reacted to the sentiment that GTA 6 is too easy.

#3473. Prince William Reportedly Wants to Strip Prince Harry of His Titles

Prince William is reportedly actively considering a plan for a “far-reaching restructuring” of the British monarchy, which he would implement once he ascends to the throne. His brother, Prince Harry, would be at the forefront of these changes: The future monarch reportedly wants only active members of the royal family who carry out duties on his behalf to retain their royal titles and the style of “Royal Highness.” These titles would therefore no longer be an “automatic privilege of birth” but would instead be equivalent to a “job title.”

The plan was detailed by Tom Sykes, a journalist and writer specializing in the royals, in his book Dukes of Hazard, to be published next February, excerpts of which were published by the Mail on Sunday on Saturday, November 21. The author, “a royal authority with impeccable society contacts” as the newspaper puts it, is said to have obtained confessions from friends of Prince William.

“If you are a working royal—going out, touring the country, doing diplomatic work, doing government work, having a public role, pressing the flesh, getting out of bed on a wet Wednesday to go to Sheffield—then you will be an HRH and you will have a prince or princess title. You will also get an allowance, a salary, and a place to live. One place to live,” the associate of the prince explained to Sykes. “If you are not doing those things and you are not a working royal, you will not get to be an HRH, you will not get a free or subsidized place to live, and you will not get any special favors. You will, however, be a private citizen free to get on with your life and make money any way you choose.”

By implementing this measure, Prince William hopes to prevent potential media scandals regarding the legitimacy of certain individuals’ right to retain their titles if they are not prominent members of the Firm (Prince Harry) or if they are under legal scrutiny (Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor). But also, and above all, the Prince of Wales hopes to offer an option to his children, Princess Charlotte, 11, and Prince Louis, eight, who could easily renounce their titles to pursue independent careers. The question does not arise for the eldest child of the Prince and Princess of Wales, Prince George, 13, whose future as heir to the throne is “guaranteed.” In fact, none of the three use their royal titles, preferring simply to be called by their first names and the surname Wales.

Under the rules established by King George V in 1917, the title of prince or princess, along with the predicate, is granted at birth to the sovereign’s children and to the children of the sovereign’s sons, as well as to all the children of the Prince of Wales’s eldest son. Prince William’s children, therefore, received these titles at birth, while Prince Harry’s children, Archie and Lilibet (ages seven and five), did not become prince and princess until King Charles III ascended the throne.

They may have to give them up if Prince William carries out his plan. “Under William’s current plan, the prince and princess titles of Harry and Meghan’s children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet, would be legally removed, along with the royal styles and princely titles of Harry and Meghan themselves,” writes Tom Sykes in his book. To do so, according to Sykes’s book, constitutional advisers have told William that he could issue letters patent, an official document authorized by the king. Such a decision could strain the relationship between the two brothers.

Sykes is convinced that Prince William would garner the approval of his subjects and “enormous public support in a country increasingly impatient with the cost and perceived excess of a sprawling royal household,” according to those close to him.

In October 2025, Prince William confided to actor Eugene Levy—whom he was hosting at Windsor Castle for the taping of Levy’s show The Reluctant Traveler—that “there are points when you look at tradition and go, Is that still fit for purpose today? Is that still the right thing to do? Are we still doing and having the most impact we could be having?”

Kensington Palace, however, declined to comment on the rumor. “As a matter of policy, we don’t comment on books or claims made within them.”

Originally published in Vanity Fair France.

#3472. Pittsburgh Steelers Announce Dramatic Aaron Rodgers News Amid Struggles

Aaron Rodgers will be spending Black Friday on the bench.

The Pittsburgh Steelers announced that Rodgers, 42, will be “inactive” against the Denver Broncos on Friday, November 27, with backup quarterback Mason Rudolph taking his spot.

The surprising move comes after two straight losses for the Steelers, both with Rodgers behind center. Pittsburgh lost in disappointing fashion to the Philadelphia Eagles, 19-16, on Sunday, November 22. Rodgers finished 30-for-44 passing with 227 yards and one touchdown.

Pittsburgh is now 6-4 on the season tied for second place in the AFC North with the Cleveland Browns. Both teams are one game behind the first-place Cincinnati Bengals.

After the loss to the Eagles, head coach Mike McCarthy scoffed at the idea of demoting Rodgers.

“Aaron Rodgers is our quarterback,” McCarthy told reporters on Monday, November 23.

However, ESPN reported on Wednesday, November 25, that the move to bench Rodgers was a coach’s decision.

Sources told NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport that Rodgers was not in attendance at the Steelers’ 8 a.m. meeting Wednesday, and it is not clear whether he will attend Wednesday’s practice at noon.

“The Steelers essentially believing that Mason Rudolph gives them the best chance to win,” Rapoport, 46, said on Wednesday. “So the big question is: What happened? Here’s my understanding of where the Steelers have been the last couple of days. They’ve had meetings — offensive meetings, staff meetings, meetings with players, meetings with Aaron Rodgers, among others — trying to figure out the best way forward, trying to figure out the issues with the offense.”

ESPN’s Steelers reporter, Brooke Pryor, called the decision to bench Rodgers “a stunning reversal.”

“Everything on Tuesday was business as usual,” Pryor, 35, explained on Wednesday. “I was in the building. They had a walk-through. It was only an hour long. If they had known at that point that they were definitively going with Mason Rudolph, safe to say that practice would have been longer than just an hour.”

Pryor said Rodgers “gave no indication that this was coming down the pipe.”

“What I can tell you is, as I was leaving the locker room at about 4:15, I saw Rodgers, Mason Rudolph and [quarterback] Will Howard sitting together in front of Mason Rudolph’s locker,” Pryor explained. “They were having a conversation. … It did feel notable because the rest of the locker room had cleared out.”

Rudolph, 31, is currently playing in his seventh NFL season, six of those with the Steelers. He has appeared in four games this season.

With Rodgers previously confirming this will be his last season, there’s a strong possibility he’s played in his final NFL game.

#3471. Another Live-Service Game Is Going Extinct, And This One Has Dinosaurs

Capcom has had a big year, but amid the hits comes news that its Overwatch-with-dinosaurs game, Exoprimal, will join the live-service graveyard next year. The game's servers will go offline next year, making it unplayable after that.

"Thank you so much for your continued use of Exoprimal, a statement on the Exoprimal site reads. "We regret to announce that service for Exoprimal will be discontinued as of Thursday, September 30, 2027. We cannot thank you enough for the love and support you have shown over the years, and we sincerely apologize for the gravity of this announcement."

Exoprimal season passes are no longer available to purchase through storefronts, and Capcom will slowly wind down the game over several months. Exoprimal and all its DLC will be delisted from stores starting March 30, 2027, but anyone who owns it can still download and play it before the September 2027 deadline. Despite a cool premise and fun gameplay, Exoprimal never truly took off after its 2023 launch.

"While Exoprimal’s early hours of repetitive and simple missions will likely drive some people away, its later surprises are a delight for those willing to give it the necessary time," James Carr wrote in GameSpot's Exoprimal review. "The escalation of difficulty and the wide variety of objectives introduced later on in the shooter gives it fresh life several hours in. Fighting through an ocean of dinosaurs is a ton of fun, and the variety of enemies keeps you from falling into a repetitive combat loop."

The writing was already on the wall for Exoprimal in 2024, as Capcom announced it was ending seasonal updates and would rotate through existing content on a monthly schedule. While that doesn't reflect the entire player community, Exoprimal numbers have largely cratered on PC via Steam: it peaked at 4,9995 concurrent players in November 2023 and nosedived the following month. At the time of writing, Exoprimal's 24-hour peak was a paltry 23 players.

2026 has been merciless for live-service games, with several high-profile casualties. Developer Wildlight’s free-to-play shooter Highguard quickly lost momentum after its January launch, Anthem was sunset this year, and New World: Aeternum began winding down operations ahead of its January 2027 closure.

#3470. The Best Tech Deals From Costco's Early Black Friday Sale

Sam's Club, Walmart, Amazon, and other retailers have been churning out early Black Friday deals since last week, so if you haven't been paying attention, you've already missed out on some good deals. But all hope is not lost: Costco recently started its own early sale, so you're still in time to find something you want at a low price. Below, I've rounded up my favorite tech deals from their sale—but keep in mind you'll need a membership to take advantage of these deals.

A powerful monitor with high-end specs can make gaming more immersive and greatly reduce input lag, which is helpful for any serious gamer looking for an edge over their opponents. The Samsung Odyssey G9 is a 49-inch gaming monitor with some impressive specs, including a 240Hz refresh rate and a 1 ms response time. It's available for $699.99 (originally $899.99), $200 off and the lowest price it has reached this year.

If you're looking for a more premium (and far more massive) gaming monitor, the 57-inch Samsung Odyssey Neo G9, one of the best ultra-wide gaming monitors on the market, is currently on sale for $1,449.99 ($2,499.99 at launch). This monitor came out in 2023, earning an "excellent" review from PCMag for its impressive 7,680 x 2,160 4K resolution, its great color range and accuracy, a 240Hz refresh rate, 1,000 nits of brightness, and its overall design. To make full use of its powerful 240Hz refresh rate, you'll need to use DisplayPort 2.1, or you'll be limited to 120Hz. You'll also need a powerful graphics card. But if you have the right setup, this thing really delivers.

The 15.3-inch Lenovo Legion is a powerful gaming laptop with premium specs, and with the current $600 discount, it's down to $1999.99 (originally $2,599.99). It has a powerful AMD Ryzen AI 9 processor, 32 GB of RAM, a GeForce RTX 5070 graphics card, and 1TB of SSD. PCMag gave the more affordable 5i version an excellent review for its price and performance, so if you have the cash for it, this one is even better.

A soundbar is a great way to improve a home entertainment system without spending too much money. This 5.1 TCL Q6CH setup is currently $199.99 (originally $299.99), including a soundbar and subwoofer. This soundbar came out in 2024 and supports Dolby Atmos and DTS:X for that 3D sound, as well as AI Sonic, a tool that tunes your sound settings based on the setup of your room.

The latest AirPods Pro are a big step up from their previous generation. The third iteration of Apple's iconic earbuds deliver a number of quality-of-life and software improvements that make them worth the typical premium over the AirPods Pro 2—and right now, the AirPods Pro 3 are even cheaper than the previous generation: They're $179 at Costco (originally $249) in an early Black Friday deal.

The 15-inch MacBook Air is down to $1,249 (originally $1,499), the lowest price since Apple hiked prices this past summer. The M5 MacBook Air is the best laptop for most people looking for a new machine in 2026. In comparison to the already excellent M4 Air, the M5 base model has double the storage, and the powerful M5 chip makes the performance even smoother, according to Mashable's review. The aluminum design is as good as you'd expect from Apple's most popular portable laptop, and it includes a Liquid Retina display, Touch ID, a 12MP Center Stage Camera, and the Magic Keyboard.

The 15.6-inch Acer Aspire Go is a great value at its current $499.99 price (originally $699.99). The display is a touchscreen; it sports an AMD Ryzen 5 processor and it has 16GB of RAM and 1TB of storage. These aren't specs you normally find at this price, making it a great laptop for anyone looking to stretch their money as far as possible while getting a workhorse of a laptop.

I'm a fan of TCL TVs, and currently own the "non-pro" version of this TV. The 65-inch QM6K Pro is $599.99 (originally $999.99) and has the same internal hardware and Mini-LED panel as the regular QM6K, but it adds a CrystGlow anti-reflective coating that makes it more viewable in well-lit rooms and helps maintain a high picture contrast. The 144 Hz native refresh rate makes gaming smooth, and support for Dolby Vision IQ, HDR10+, HDR10, and HLG means you're well positioned to get the best sound quality when streaming movies or shows.

Nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Black Friday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, November 30, 2026. The “best” sales depend on your needs, but in general, the biggest discounts tend to come from larger retailers who can afford lower prices: think places like Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and Home Depot. You can find all the best sales from major retailers on our Black Friday coverage.

Yes, Apple participates in Black Friday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

I'm a hardcore reality TV fan, and this year is my first time watching a full season of The Great British Baking Show with my Netflix subscription. While longtime fans have been criticizing its twists or coming after the way Nigella Lawson eats, I've had a total blast watching the heartwarming competition series. Although I will say I totally called out a problem from Day 1 that ended up having a big impact on the semifinals episode.

Following Connie's truly heartbreaking elimination, the semifinal episode of Bake Off featured the top four contestants creating Patisseries. There was just one big problem: the heat wave in the U.K. was making it especially hot in the iconic tent. Unfortunately that threw a wrench into the baker's plans, especially when they needed the time to cool their bakes. I thought this was going to be a big problem over the course of the season, and I feel totally vindicated after watching the semifinal episode of the season.

The struggle of cooling bakes has been a recurring theme throughout this season of Bake Off, and it had major implications during Patisserie week. This was especially true for the technical challenge, where contestants needed to create judge Paul Hollywood's Gateau Concorde in 21⁄2 hours. Inside the tent was reportedly a whopping 94 degrees, and a number of the bakes suffered as a result.

Unfortunately, Gabe struggled quite a bit during the semifinals, partially thanks to the heat and his bakes not being able to properly cool. He ended up being eliminated before the finals, but he wasn't the only one who had issues with the heat while trying to craft his patisseries. Frontrunner Tom's babas were also underproofed, so it was clear that the heat wave was affecting the whole cast. I can't imagine how it must have felt to be so hot while baking, especially because I also tend to overheat when experiencing anxiety.

There's just one episode for this season of The Great British Baking Show, so the pressure is on for the final there bakers to stick the landing and hopefully pull out a W. While fans across the pond already know who will take the prize, we here in the states will have to wait until Black Friday to stream the finale episode on Netflix. I'm especially curious to see if the U.K. heatwave from last summer continues to be a menace for the contestants during their final few bakes. Can't we get some better air conditioning in the Bake Off tent?

#3468. Diablo 4’s Most Nostalgic Season Is Becoming (Mostly) Permanent

Diablo 4 is gearing up for the arrival of Season 16, but it won't be leaving its popular previous season behind entirely.

As detailed by Blizzard in a breakdown of the upcoming Season of Tyrael's Gambit, much of the previous season, Hell's Legacy, will become a permanent part of Diablo 4 going forward. Season 15 served as celebration of the franchise's history, and added a smorgasbord of items and callbacks to previous Diablo titles, including a storyline revolving around Deckard Cain and the return of enemies and boss encounters from Diablo 2. 

Most of that is carrying forward, Blizzard said. Due to "overwhelming requests" from the game's community, Blizzard outlined what all from Hell's Legacy will survive.

Hell's Legacy's capstone dungeons will be added, as will the ability to summon a World Boss version of Diablo and take on the cow god Moopisto. The Prime Evil Council is also becoming permanent, and will work the same way the game's other Lair bosses do, with players needing a specific item to open their reward chest after successfully defeating the encounter.

Waking Nightmare dungeons will still be accessible, but only by finding Chronicle of Nightmares dungeon keys. Monsters from previous Diablo games will also have a chance to spawn in The Pit. Those who progressed their secret cow level journey can also rejoice, as the secret cow island and its corresponding waypoint will be staying.

Many of Hell's Legacy's best items were new versions of classics from older Diablo games, and those Legacy Uniques will be added permanently as well, including the Annihilus Seal and Hellfire Torch Charm.

That's all for now, but Blizzard said more of Hell's Legacy could make a return in the future.

"Other popularly requested features are being evaluated for rework and may appear in the future," Blizzard said.

Diablo 4 Season 16 launches December 1. In addition to bringing forward much of Hell's Legacy, Tyrael's Gambit will additionally overhaul the game's War Plans system and make its Helltide activity easier.

Diablo 4 won't receive new expansions going forward, but it is receiving a new class, the Amazon, next year. Blizzard is also hard at work on Diablo 5. Though it's not slated to arrive until 2029, Blizzard has already revealed three of Diablo 5's playable classes and promised it will launch with more class options than any previous Diablo game.

#3467. The Return of Malin Akerman and Brittany Snow’s Twisted ‘Hunting Wives’ Love Story

In 2021, at the recommendation of a film producer, the writer and showrunner Rebecca Cutter read a pulpy murder-mystery novel on a flight from her native Massachusetts to her current base in Los Angeles. By the time she landed, Cutter had finished the book and was already mapping out the TV adaptation in her head.

The plot heavily involved a Texas abortion clinic, and the state had just passed SB 8, one of the country’s most restrictive abortion bills until Roe v. Wade was overturned the following year. As she contemplated bringing The Hunting Wives to life, Cutter saw the political stakes come into focus as well.

“I started thinking about the ‘red state, blue state’ of it,” she tells Vanity Fair ahead of the show’s season two premiere on Thursday. “What if…we really play this culture war?”

“I don’t think I do gratuitous sex scenes,” says showrunner Rebecca Cutter. “I think you always are seeing a power dynamic play out or a plot point play out.”

The result was one of Netflix’s biggest breakout hits in recent years, sent up in a Saturday Night Live sketch as the “straight but lesbian, horny Republican murder drama.” As a show, Hunting Wives amps up the noirish aspects of the suspense thriller written by May Cobb, a native of the East Texas Piney Woods, and adds a heaping dose of MAGA-adjacent camp. Cutter finishes the mix with plenty of sex scenes, particularly between Malin Akerman’s Margo, a femme fatale partly inspired by Melania Trump who is married to a Republican gubernatorial hopeful, and Brittany Snow’s Sophie, a liberal do-gooder who, like Cutter, arrives in town from a blue corner of Massachusetts. (Cutter was raised in Cambridge and graduated from Wesleyan University, the Connecticut liberal arts college known for its progressive politics and pipeline to Hollywood.)

Hunting Wives executive producer Erwin Stoff told Cutter he’d pay for her to go to Texas to meet Cobb and breathe the Piney Woods air herself. She met Cobb’s father and her best friend from high school. She shot skeet with the women—she even got it in three, just as Sophie does in the first season. At a high-end Dallas shopping area where the likes of Gucci can be found, Cutter got a better sense of the hair, clothes, and bodies of her eventual characters. “I understand the notion that Sophie could be amused and entertained and intrigued by these women,” Cutter says, “and eventually seduced.”

Cutter thinks of the show primarily in terms of its tonal mash-up: “I think we managed to wrangle it into one piece of art,” she says, “but there’s comedy, there’s violence, there’s noir, there’s soap, there’s earnest emotion.” To the extent that she assigned any political beliefs to the rich white women of Cobb’s novel, it was in the spirit of grounding her characters in the specifics of their world. Still, as we speak, Cutter decides “to get real with it.”

Cutter on set. She describes Sophie, a fellow native of blue Massachusetts, as a surrogate for her own awakening to MAGA Texas.

“The whole thing was a little bit of a parable, in my mind, of how you could fall for someone like [Donald] Trump,” she admits. “Sophie has her principles, but they only go so far. They end right where something starts to make her feel good.” Cutter was as curious as anyone else from her educated milieu about the quirkier aspects of Trump, like the Diet Coke button he had installed on the Resolute Desk. How liberating must it feel to embrace a movement so openly untethered from the pieties of politics and taste?

“Not that my show is a deep dive on Trump,” Cutter says, “but maybe there is an element that’s sort of looking under the hood.”

The twisted love story between Margo and Sophie entangles all of the wealthy, hard-drinking, gun-toting women in their orbit, and its central killing—one of several propelling the show forward, with a third season slated to begin filming this year—stems from an effort to cover up Margo’s abortion as her NRA-loving husband plots his political ascent. (In this proudly oversexed town, he has his own share of affairs.) Hunting Wives is the rare Netflix soap to receive steady coverage from mainstream national outlets; the fascination undoubtedly has something to do with the impression that, like Yellowstone or Morgan Wallen before it, the show unlocks something about MAGA’s cultural staying power. In a New York Times guest essay this month that evaluated the post-2024 Hollywood landscape, Sharon Waxman, the editor in chief of The Wrap, wrote, “From Melania on Amazon’s streaming service to The Hunting Wives on Netflix to the ever-expanding Taylor Sheridan universe on Paramount+ to Bari Weiss’s being put in charge of CBS News, the vibe shift was visible on all our screens.”

Margo and her politically ambitious husband are partners in subterfuge and debauchery.

Cutter says she had no particular agenda nor any “ultra-evil villain plan of how it was going to be received or how it would be culturally relevant.” But Hunting Wives is sprinkled with enough proper nouns—a Peter Thiel mention here, a Walmart reference there—and distinctly modern aesthetics that she can acknowledge its appeal as something of a Rosetta stone for the moment in MAGA femininity. Even in the ostensibly waning days of the movement, the plastic surgery and soaring heels continue to captivate and horrify coastal elites. Cutter says that Callie (Jaime Ray Newman), another of Margo’s lovers, has a bit of Kristi Noem and Marjorie Taylor Greene in her: that “sort of slightly butch, real gun, real ‘back the blue’ [element]…the toughness of those women.”

The second season of Hunting Wives maintains the slipperiness that keeps the show from veering into moralism; it stands apart from other Trump-era art in its refusal to take sides. “I think I remember, in the pitch, someone saying, ‘But will red-state people like it too?’” Cutter recalls. “I was like, ‘I think so.’” Both Margo and Sophie are awash in their respective red and blue stereotypes, but neither is more admirable than the other. Their sordid union is a testament to the flexibility of both their principles and their preferences. From one vantage, it is, in the end, all about sex.

“Margo is the symbol of freedom and sexuality and feminine power and empoweredness and selfishness that [Sophie] feels she’s lost,” Cutter says, adding that Akerman’s comfort in such a role helped drive her liberal use of physical intimacy. “The audience may disagree with me,” she says, but “I don’t think I do gratuitous sex scenes. I think you always are seeing a power dynamic play out or a plot point play out.” Last year, though, when Netflix acquired Hunting Wives, which was initially ordered by Starz in 2023, Cutter had a more practical concern.

“I literally googled,” she recalls, “‘Does Netflix show boobs?’”

#3466. Three Years After His Death, EA Is Using AI To Bring Back A Famed Commentator In FC 27

EA Sports FC 27 is adding an AI-generated commentator for the first time in the series' history, with famed British commentator John Motson having his voice synthesized for the football title.

Motson, who passed way in 2023, previously provided commentary for EA's FIFA series, appearing in the game's first iteration in 1996 and featuring until 2005. According to the BBC, EA approached Motson's wife and son for permission to regenerate his voice and use his likeness for this year's entry in the series. Both agreed to the idea, but neither party has disclosed how much EA has paid for the use. Fred Motson, John's son, stated that he believed his father would've approved of this use of AI.

"My dad was the least technological person in the world," Fred stated. "Till his dying day, he had a typewriter on his desk. So I don't think he would have quite understood what the AI was doing technologically, but I think, on the other hand, he was always really keen to get involved in these kinds of projects."

Peter Caulfield, founder of Save Our Voices Now, which campaigns against this exact use of AI, questions whether a family should be able to provide consent for someone who can no longer give it themselves. "If someone has signed a deal allowing their likeness to be used after they die, I have no issue with that," he explained. "But in life or in death, unless you have specifically agreed to it, AI cloning of any kind should not be allowed. Being a family member shouldn't automatically give you that right either."

This isn't new to video games, either. Epic Games used a similar method to bring back the late James Earl Jones' voice for its Star Wars event in Fortnite, with the actor's estate agreeing to the use. It allowed players to converse with the AI bot while playing, and was very quickly removed after some users managed to get the bot to spew out racist or vulgar phrases, all delivered with the voice of Jones. It also drew the ire of SAG-AFTRA, which claimed that Epic had violated labor practices.

Derek Rae, one of the currently employed commentators on EA Sports FC 27, said he was excited by the inclusion of Motson's voice, and that he didn't believe AI was yet going to replace his own work on the game. When asked whether he would make the same decision to have his work endure for years to come through AI, he replied, "I'm hopefully many years away from having to make a decision like that."

#3465. These XGIMI Projectors Are up to 40% Off Ahead of Black Friday

I've been using the XGIMI MoGo 3 Pro since it came out in 2024 and have been recommending it to friends and family every chance I get. It quickly became my favorite portable projector, and two years later, it's still my go-to for a spontaneous projector session. If you're on the lookout for a good deal on a portable projector, I recommend considering the following XGIMI deals.

If you're looking for the most affordable option, the Vibe One projector is just $179 (originally $299) after a 40% discount. This is a 1080p resolution and 1500:1 contrast portable projector for casual watching at night with 250 ISO lumens of brightness, and the price reflects that. It already comes with Google TV, which is my favorite OS, so you can download and stream any app you want. It's battery-powered, which means you can take it anywhere with you (as long as you have wifi). The battery lasts up to 1.2 hours for projecting video (in Eco Mode), and up to four hours as a speaker (it has built-in dual 3W JBL speakers). The auto keystone from XGIMI is one of the best ones I've experienced among all of the projectors I've tested, and it will adjust to practically any surface you cast it on, which can, with the 160° adjustable built-in stand, even be the ceiling. The current bundle brings an 80-inch screen included in the price.

If you have a bit more money to splurge, the MoGo 4 is the same concept as the Vibe One but takes its specs to the next level, and it's available starting at $359 (originally $499). It's still small and compact with 1080p resolution, but it nearly doubles the brightness, with 450 ISO lumens. The battery life more than doubles to two and a half hours in Eco Mode, while still keeping the projector under three pounds. It also has Google TV as its OS, but the projection is 360° with its adjustable built-in stand. You also have the option of getting the bundle with the PowerBase Stand, which extends the battery to five hours. Like the Vibe One, it has a built-in speaker, but this one uses dual 6W Harman Kardon speakers with Dolby Audio.The MoGo 4 Laser is a slightly upgraded version that uses triple laser technology for a better picture. It still supports 1080p resolution, but it's brighter with 550 ISO lumens and a 1000:1 contrast. The battery life, OS system, stand, speakers, and auto keystone technology are the same—but the bundles are different, so they're worth considering if they fit your needs.

If you're looking for a premium portable projector, the Horizon 30 Pro is a great option that competes with the best options on the market. It supports 4K resolution, uses RGB triple laser brightness that reaches 4800 ISO lumens (bright enough to see during the day), has a 120Hz refresh rate and gaming features to make gaming smooth, displays an 8,000:1 native contrast to make colors and blacks pop, and supports IMAX Enhanced, Dolby Vision, and HDR10+. It has an adjustable stand like the other XGIMI projectors and its own dual 12W Harman Kardon speakers with DTS Virtual:X and DTS-HD. The auto keystone is just as powerful as the other options, but the lens adds an optical zoom and a Lens Memory feature, which lets you save up to six custom lens and image setups and recall them with a click. Right now, it's down to $1,899 (originally $2,499) after a 24% discount.
